walkthroughs.body_html:
Finance and Accounts — a core area of Business Studies.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Finance and Accounts brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Finance and Accounts.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Luca Pacioli's 'Summa de Arithmetica' detailing double-entry bookkeeping dates from:

options: Payback
Average rate of return
Net present value
Accounting rate
Shareholders' personal assets are protected if the company fails — they can only lose the amount they invested, not their personal wealth.
Limited liability means a business can only operate for a limited time.
Operations management is only about manufacturing factories.
Limited liability means the company has limited debts it can take on.

mcqs.q: What is operations management concerned with?
options: Limited liability means a business can only operate for a limited time.
Operations management is only about manufacturing factories.
The design and control of the production process and business operations — converting inputs into outputs efficiently. It includes capacity, quality, supply chain, and process improvement.
Operations management is the same as general management.
